A1.justification: Despite the changed title and expanded theoretical scope, the authors, retained MAE framework, proofs, and experiments establish that these are versions of the same work. Both PDFs, including their figures, equations, and complete appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 reports an original attention-diversity analysis of four pretrained ViT-B/16 models across 152 images, with results in Figure 2.

after.justification: Section 7 retains the original attention-diversity analysis and its results, now displayed in Figure 3. Retained empirical results still qualify.

M1.justification: v3 adds an analyzed contrastive-learning transformer with position-to-content attention, average-pooled outputs, masked positive pairs, stop-gradient handling, and a regularized contrastive objective (Section 2.4). v2 specifies only the masked-reconstruction model and objective, which v3 retains.

E1.justification: Empirical coverage remains the attention analysis of ImageNet-1K-pretrained vision transformers on the same 152 example images. The new noisy contrastive-learning distribution is a theoretical assumption, not an experimentally evaluated dataset or scenario.

E2.justification: The attention-diversity comparison retains MAE, MoCo v3, DINO, and DeiT. Figure 1 retains the same MAE, MoCo, and DINO attention maps. The newly formulated theoretical CL model is not added as an empirical comparator.

E3.justification: v2 Section 6 and v3 Section 7 retain ViT-B/16, its 12 final-layer attention heads, 152 images, top-10 attended patches, and the same coordinate-distance metric. Changing the patch-grid notation from P to N does not change the protocol.

E4.justification: The illustrative attention maps and per-head diversity analysis are retained. Neither version adds or removes empirical ablations, robustness tests, or sensitivity studies; the new contrastive-learning analyses are mathematical derivations.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same boxplots to describe variation across images. There are no changes to repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance testing. The new theoretical probability bounds are not uncertainty estimates for empirical results.

E6.justification: Figure 1's attention maps and the attention-diversity plot in v2 Figure 2/v3 Figure 3 are unchanged. The displayed distributions and finding that MAE has greater attention diversity are retained, with no added or revised empirical result entries.

T1.justification: v3 adds the CL convergence and global-attention-collapse theorem (Theorem 4.4), Gaussian-noise assumptions, and supporting derivations in Appendix B. Definition 2.1 changes K from O(1) to O(polylog(P)); Theorem 4.2 changes the MAE correlation bound from O(log(P)/η) to O(log(P/ε)). The earlier MAE proofs are largely retained and reorganized.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion expand from explaining masked reconstruction to claiming convergence guarantees and contrasting learned attention patterns for both MAE and CL. The central contribution now includes CL's global attention collapse even under mild feature imbalance.

C2.justification: v3 extends the existing MAE interpretation with a mechanism for CL collapse: global features receive larger initial gradients, and learning them suffices for the contrastive objective without position-specific local reconstruction. It also explains the CL-specific embedding simplification and introduction of noisy data.

D1.justification: For the newly analyzed CL procedure, v3 supplies parameter prescriptions including noise variance σ0²=1/d, temperature τ=O(1/log d), and regularization conditions in Appendix B. These add theoretical setup details; the retained empirical implementation and code/data-access disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: The existing literature survey largely remains. v3 adds references to CLIP, Cambrian-1, Ji et al.'s contrastive-feature theory, and Yang et al.'s in-context learning analysis, while shortening the detailed JSL22/PZS22 comparisons and adapting the positioning to joint MAE/CL theory.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are substantially rewritten around the two SSL objectives. v2 Appendix A becomes the main-text proof overview in v3 Section 5; v2 Appendices B–G are consolidated into Appendix A. Related work and experiments exchange order.

P2.justification: All four graphics are retained. The data-distribution and attention-diversity figures exchange numbering and placement, the mechanism figure moves alongside the main results, and captions are revised. These are presentation changes without new plots or tables.

improvement.justification: The broader MAE/CL comparison and reorganized exposition offer useful explanatory gains, but the central new proof contains unresolved inconsistencies. Lemma B.2 uses the regularization term λΦ, whereas Appendix B.3 uses Φ/λ; the gradient-descent squared-distance identity on page 62 also reverses the distance-term signs. These directly affect support for the added convergence claim, preventing a reliable net quality judgment from the supplied PDFs.
